::: {.lead-statement}
Physics-based micromechanical modeling with crystal plasticity for failure prediction in advanced high-strength steels.
:::

I develop computational models that connect microstructure to failure in advanced high-strength steels. My work combines **crystal plasticity**, **damage mechanics**, **high-rate experiments**, **EBSD/DIC/IR measurements**, and **finite element implementation** to predict stress-strain softening, temperature rise, void evolution, texture change, and failure. The goal is practical: reduce trial-and-error testing and build validated simulation tools for crash-critical lightweight steel design and future ML-based FLD prediction.

I am completing my PhD in Mechanical and Mechatronics Engineering at the [University of Waterloo](https://uwaterloo.ca/). My current work focuses on thermodynamically consistent crystal-plasticity damage modeling for HSLA, DP, and Q&P steels, with direct relevance to automotive forming, crashworthiness, and material model calibration.

## Research Focus

::: {.research-grid}
::: {.research-card}
### Crystal Plasticity Damage
Thermodynamically consistent damage evolution coupled with rate-dependent crystal plasticity for polycrystalline steels.
:::

::: {.research-card}
### High-Rate Failure
Prediction of void nucleation, growth, coalescence, post-necking softening, and fracture under dynamic loading.
:::

::: {.research-card}
### Thermo-Mechanical Coupling
Internal heat generation from plastic dissipation, local temperature rise, and its effect on dislocation recovery and softening.
:::

::: {.research-card}
### ML-Ready FLD Direction
Physics-based features and validated simulation data that can support machine-learning prediction of forming limit behavior.
:::
:::

## Featured Work

::: {.feature-panel}
::: {.feature-copy}
### Crystal plasticity-based damage model for HSLA steels
Published in *International Journal of Plasticity*, this work developed and validated a rate-dependent crystal-plasticity damage model for HR340 and HR550 steels. The model captures stress-strain response, temperature rise, texture evolution, damage accumulation, and intermediate strain-rate predictions.

[Read the research page](research.qmd){.btn-link-primary} [Paper DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijplas.2025.104255){.btn-link}
:::
